_doc: PW2 -- the AUTHORED half of the self-clearing-alarm census. The hits are DERIVED by background/self_clearing_alarm_census.py (writer set intersected with reader set per state path, over background/ and tools/); this file records the judgement on each. A hit with no row here, or a 'benign' row with no reason, makes `--check` exit 1 -- so a newly-written control of this shape lands RED instead of joining the class quietly.
_scope_note: All 6 real hits are GUARDED as of 2026-08-10 (PW2 built the census and guarded .publish_gate_state.json, the instance the steer was about; PW4 chose the close condition for, and guarded, the next four; the sixth, publish_provenance.json, arrived already guarded on 2026-08-10 -- its author reached the once-only-stamp property independently, which is the census working as intended: the class was known before the control was written). Each close condition is NAMED in its own module and INDEPENDENT of the state file it closes (R15 anti-tautology): a pytest pass count, a filesystem-derived work key, the maturity map's own level/stage, a publisher return code. They were deliberately not guarded in one pass -- 'what evidences an episode close' is a per-control judgement, and guarding by reflex with a condition nobody chose produces controls that can never clear, which is the accretion OPERATIONAL_COHERENCE_DESIGN_PASS forbids. `--check` now fails on a `real` row that is not `guarded` with a test citation that exists on disk, so the guard field cannot decay into prose nobody checks.

_verdicts._scope_of_benign: BENIGN ANSWERS ONE QUESTION: can a write SHORTEN an episode? It is not a clean bill of health for the file. In particular it says nothing about whether the carrier's LOADER tells ABSENT from PRESENT-BUT-UNREADABLE -- a seen-set, a watermark or a read-modify-write store can be perfectly benign on the episode question and still destroy data, or crash, when its state file is corrupt. Rows swept for that carry a `loader` field saying what the answer is, and the sweep is ranked by what the carrier's WRITER does: a read-modify-write over the whole record can DESTROY the record on a corrupt read, where a pure reader only loses a suppression or spends a cycle. A row without one has not been asked, which is a gap and not a pass.
_verdicts.benign: The path carries no episode-scoped field, so no write can shorten an episode. A latest-value watermark, a once-per-period guard, a seen-set, or an append-only log. The reason is mandatory.
_verdicts.real: The path carries an EPISODE-SCOPED field -- an episode-start timestamp or a consecutive-failure counter -- that an alarm reads for SEVERITY, and a write that has not demonstrated the episode ended can shorten or reset it. Requires the append-or-monotonic guard (background/episode_monotonic.py).

.atom_stall_tracker.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. Already on `load_episode_prior`. Same as `.supervisor_stuck_state.json`.
.atom_stall_tracker.json.why: `consecutive_unchanged` per atom is an episode counter, and _record_atom_draw_and_check_stall writes the same field its own stall check reads. The episode closed on ANY fingerprint difference, and two of the five fingerprint components change without the atom advancing -- an `expert_hour.last` re-stamp (which IS the livelock the tracker exists to catch, resetting the counter meant to catch it) and a `level_target` re-plan. CLOSE CONDITION (PW4): level_current changed, loop_stage changed, or simplifications_count went UP -- the atom's own advancing state in docs/design/maturity_map.yaml, read from the map at draw time and never from this file. Guarded via supervisor._atom_fingerprint_progressed + guard_episode(streak_fields=ATOM_STALL_STREAK_FIELDS). Replay proof: tests/background/test_pw4_episode_guards.py::test_stall_an_expert_hour_restamp_does_not_reset_the_streak (opposite direction: ::test_stall_real_progress_still_closes_the_episode).

.boot_announced.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. Not JSON. `already_announced_this_boot` compares stripped text to the boot id under `except OSError`; no parse, so no partition. Every corrupt content answers False -- fails open to announcing twice, never to silence. Writer overwrites.
.boot_announced.why: A single boot timestamp used as a once-only announce guard. No episode, no counter.

.daily_self_note_last_date.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. Same shape as `.boot_announced`: `already_ran_today` is a stripped text compare against today's date under `except OSError`. Fails open to running the note again.
.daily_self_note_last_date.why: A date stamp gating one note per day. Latest-value by design; carries no episode length.

.dispatcher_seen.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-04. `_load_seen` was annotated `-> dict[str, str]` under `except (json.JSONDecodeError, Exception)` -- which is only `except Exception` -- and returned `None` for `null` and a LIST for `[1, 2, 3]`; both PARSE, so the except-clause never saw them, and the caller's next line is `seen[path.name] = classification`. The `{}` rows are the destructive half and why this row was ranked first: it is a read-modify-write, so `{}` is not a lost suppression -- the next `_save_seen` writes it back and every from_rich already classified and routed becomes unseen, is re-classified and is re-routed and re-notified. That is the stale-from_rich re-jam arriving by a different door. Repaired via `episode_prior.load_episode_prior`; `main` preserves the bytes before the first save. A mapping with unknown keys stays READABLE deliberately -- a seen-map's keys are arbitrary filenames, so there is no schema to violate. Control: tests/background/test_the_two_read_modify_write_seen_carriers.py
.dispatcher_seen.json.why: A seen-set keyed by filename. Append-only in effect -- entries are added, never used to measure how long anything has been failing.

.harden_cooldown.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). Same shape as `.wedge_suspect_hit_rate.json`: the loader's fail-open to {} is argued for in its own docstring and is right (a broken marker must never silence a real HARDEN draw), but `record_harden_pass` is a read-modify-write over that {}. Measured against a live prior of 8 atoms: every unreadable state loaded 0 and the next stamp would write a ONE-atom marker over all 8, turning a temporary fail-open into a permanent loss -- recently-hardened atoms silently re-offered. Repaired with `preserve_unreadable` in the WRITER only; the loader has pure readers (`_is_drained_and_gated`, `deadmans_switch._rest_is_proven_legitimate`) that must not move bytes about. `_load_harden_cooldown` also moved to `load_episode_prior` so the screen is the shared one. `{"a": 1}` stays READABLE: the keys are arbitrary atom ids, so there is no schema to violate -- same reasoning as the dispatcher seen-map.
.harden_cooldown.json.why: A cooldown stamp recording when a HARDEN pass last ran. Latest-value; nothing reads it as an episode.

.last_gate_blocking_tests.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. `last_red_census` is exemplary and needs nothing: it screens `isinstance(rec, dict)`, the timestamp type, the age AND the enum membership, and every unreadable shape answers `fail_fast_only` -- the verdict that makes no completeness claim. Live prior ('complete', 3); all seven answer ('fail_fast_only', 0).
.last_gate_blocking_tests.json.why: The last RED gate's blocking pytest node ids ({ts, git_hash, node_ids}) -- the one fact that identifies a wedge, published across the process boundary because the alarm runs elsewhere. Flagged because _write_blocking_tests is on the publish FAILURE path and _fire_publish_gate_alert reads it, but it carries NO episode-scoped field: no episode start, no consecutive-failure counter. Episode severity comes from .publish_gate_state.json and nothing here. Overwriting it with the CURRENT red's node ids is the mechanism (a stale red must never be citable against a later failure -- a green gate deletes it outright), and its age fails in the SAFE direction: past GATE_BLOCKING_TESTS_MAX_AGE_SECONDS it reads as UNRECORDED and the alarm says so, which makes the page say LESS rather than making an episode look shorter.

.last_processed_fingerprint.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-04, measured, no repair needed and this row says why rather than assuming it. `_read_last_fingerprint` returns None for an absent file and None for a corrupt one -- the same conflation in form -- but the only consumer is `last_fp == fingerprint` on the change-detection gate, and EVERY member of the partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/bare string/list) compares unequal and therefore forces a republish. Nothing raises: the comparison is `==`, not an index. So the fail direction is toward publishing, which is the safe one, and the cost of an unreadable file is one extra regen cycle rather than a silent SKIP on stale figures. It is a pure reader -- the writer stamps a freshly computed fingerprint and never reads the file back -- so a corrupt read cannot destroy a record either.
.last_processed_fingerprint.json.why: The fingerprint of the last processed run, for idempotence (don't republish an unchanged run). Latest-value by design; no severity derived.

.last_publish_cause.json.loader: SURFACED 2026-09-05 by the census parameter-seam repair: this path was a hit all along and the census could not see it, because its read happens behind a path-taking helper. Dispositioned on first sight, not back-dated. ASKED AND CLEAN, and it is the best loader in the census. `publish_cause.read_cause` splits FileNotFoundError from JSONDecodeError/OSError/ValueError from `not isinstance(rec, dict)` from an unusable `ts`, and returns UNATTRIBUTED with A DIFFERENT NAMED SENTENCE for each -- absent and unreadable are told apart and the reader is told which. `null` and [1,2,3] land on the not-a-dict branch; `"abc"` likewise. Nothing raises, and the writer overwrites the whole record. Nothing to repair.
.last_publish_cause.json.why: The attributed cause of a publish that did not land -- {cause, evidence, ts, git_hash}, written by `git_commit_push` on one of its four rc=77 paths and read by `record_publish_gate_outcome` in a LATER process. Latest-value and keyed to its own commit AND age-bounded (`max_age`), so a stale record is refused rather than carried: it cannot lengthen or shorten an episode because it does not describe one. The episode clock for this alarm lives in `.publish_gate_state.json`, which is the `real` instance.

.last_push_time.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. `_push_due` catches KeyError AND TypeError, so `null['ts']`, `[1,2]['ts']` and `'abc'['ts']` are all caught by the TypeError leg. Live prior answers False (throttled); every unreadable state answers True. Fails open to pushing, which is the safe direction, and the writer overwrites a single timestamp.
.last_push_time.json.why: {"ts": ...} of the last successful push -- a latest-SUCCESS stamp, so a failure never writes it. Liveness is measured as time SINCE this value, which a failure cannot shorten.

.last_tested_hash.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED. A bare git sha as text. A corrupt value simply does not equal the current HEAD, so `_green_is_on_record_for` answers 'not proven green' -- the fail-CLOSED direction, and identical to what an absent file gives. Deliberately conflated and correctly so.
.last_tested_hash.why: Written ONLY on a gate PASS, never on a failure, so no failure path touches it. It is load-bearing in the opposite direction: the wedge draw reads it as the INDEPENDENT anti-tautology cross-check (a pass at HEAD means the failures are stale). Changing it to record failures would DESTROY that independence.

.lock.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED. NOT A STATE RECORD -- an flock sentinel whose CONTENT is never parsed; the file's existence and the kernel lock are the whole payload. There is no absent-vs-unreadable partition to measure. Census hit is a false positive of the path derivation; left as a row rather than removed, so the next sweep does not re-derive and re-ask it.
.lock.why: NOT AN ALARM STATE FILE -- a mutex. The key comes from process_run_complete.PYTEST_TEMP_LOCK_NAME = '.lock', a bare dotfile which _state_key classifies as state under its 'a dotfile with no suffix is state too' rule (the same rule that correctly catches .last_tested_hash). The file's entire content is the holding session's PID, written when a numbered pytest temp root is claimed and unlinked from an atexit hook; the sibling REUSED_HEAD_CHECKOUT_LOCK_NAME and RUN_LOCK_FILE are the same shape. Its lifecycle is acquire/release, not accumulate/clear: there is no episode-start timestamp and no consecutive-failure counter, so no write can shorten an episode, because no episode is stored. It reaches a notifier only transitively -- _pytest_root_holder and _sweep_stale_pytest_temp_roots sit inside process_run_complete, which notifies about the RUN, never about the lock. The census is right to surface it (a lock is written and read by the same module) and right not to decide it; deciding it is what this row is for.

.maintenance_reminder_sent.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. `_load_maintenance_state`'s `except (JSONDecodeError, Exception)` IS `except Exception`, which reads as a defect and is not one here -- the `.get` on a non-mapping raises inside it. Live prior '2026-08'; every unreadable state answers ''. Pure reader over a single-key record the writer fully overwrites, so the cost is one re-queued monthly reminder.
.maintenance_reminder_sent.json.why: A once-per-month reminder guard. A latest-sent stamp with no severity derived from it.

.notify_transitions.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-04. `_read_transitions` is annotated `-> dict` and returned None for a file containing `null`, one `.get` away from every caller. Absent and unreadable remain the same ANSWER, deliberately: this memory only suppresses a REPEAT, so losing it costs one duplicate message and never a missed one. Control: tests/background/test_benign_rows_were_never_asked_the_loader_question.py
.notify_transitions.json.why: R5 transition memory: per-key {state, ts} recording the last state notified, so an unchanged status is not re-sent. The stored value is the latest state by design -- overwriting it is the mechanism, not a defect -- and no severity is derived from its age.

.ntfy_delivery_state.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED. Already classified -- `ntfy_utils.delivery_state_classified` returns `(state, verdict)` and its docstring names ABSENT and PRESENT-BUT-UNREADABLE as opposite facts. Asked and answered before this sweep.
.ntfy_delivery_state.json.why: `since_epoch` is a deafness-episode START and `consecutive_failures` is its LENGTH; both are written by ntfy_utils.record_delivery_outcome on the failure path and are the fields any deafness alarm (the finding's part 3, not yet built) would read for SEVERITY -- so an unearned reset would page a multi-hour silent-escalation outage as a fresh one, the class's own cardinal sin. CLOSE CONDITION: ntfy returned a server-assigned message id for this POST -- the strongest evidence this channel can produce, read off the SERVER's response body and never off this state file (R15 anti-tautology). `since_epoch` is NUMERIC deliberately: guard_episode's water-marks are numeric-only and skip a string silently (WORKER_FINDING_THE_MONOTONIC_GUARD_IS_NUMERIC_ONLY, an open BLOCKING member of the controls-that-cannot-fail class), so an ISO `since` alone would be a guard that cannot fire; the readable `since` is kept alongside it, unguarded and not load-bearing. Guarded via episode_monotonic.guard_episode(since_fields=('since_epoch',), streak_fields=('consecutive_failures',), episode_closed=delivered). Replay proof: tests/background/test_ntfy_utils.py::test_an_open_deafness_episode_cannot_be_shortened (opposite direction: ::test_a_real_delivery_does_close_the_episode).

.ntfy_digest_state.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). `_read_state` was `except Exception: return {}`, which caught the truncated file and NOT `null` / `[1,2,3]` / `"abc"`; those parse, so `pending()`'s `.get` raised AttributeError and nothing flushed at all. The {} half is not a lost suppression but a REPLAY: `digested_through_seq` reads 0, so measured against a live prior of 5 pending in a 30-entry queue, `pending()` returned all 30 -- the watermark is the only thing between a corrupt read and the director receiving every notification this daemon has ever deferred. Repaired via `load_episode_prior`. NOT preserved and NOT alarmed, deliberately: the next successful flush rewrites the watermark from the entries it actually carried, so the record self-repairs, and a 30-message digest announces itself.
.ntfy_digest_state.json.why: The high-water mark of what a CONFIRMED digest flush has carried (notification_digest G-N5), held deliberately SEPARATE from the queue so the record of what was said and the record of what was sent cannot corrupt each other. Flagged because _write_state() full-rewrites it on the notification path. It is the INVERSE of this class rather than an instance of it: the write happens only inside `if _was_delivered(result)`, so the FAILURE path (429, curl failure, or any pytest/suppressed/test_fixture sentinel) writes NOTHING and leaves the mark exactly where it was -- the undelivered items ride the next digest instead of evaporating. Neither key is an episode clock an alarm reads for severity: `digested_through_seq` is a max() over the entries just delivered and therefore monotonic, and `last_digest_ts` stamps the last SUCCESSFUL flush, so neither can be reset by a failure to shorten a measured outage.

.ntfy_responder_seen_hashes.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-04 and it is the one defect the sweep has found that leaves the daemon UP and answering nothing. `_load_seen_hashes` was `json.loads` under `except (JSONDecodeError, ValueError)`, annotated `-> list[str]`; `null`, `{"a": 1}` and `"abc"` all parse, so none reached the except. Measured against a live prior of three hashes, following the value into `check_once`: null -> None -> TypeError at `set(seen_hashes)`; a mapping -> membership tested its KEYS then AttributeError at `.append`; a bare string -> a SUBSTRING test then AttributeError. `main()` binds the list ONCE and re-passes the same object every cycle, so the raise recurs on every poll inside its own `except Exception`, and a restart re-reads the same file: the responder polls forever, answers nothing, and `since` never advances. Empty and truncated were the read-modify-write half -- the whole record lost and written back one cycle later. REPAIRED via episode_prior.load_list_prior (item-typed), the bytes preserved through the new shared `preserve_unreadable`, and `_save_seen_hashes` made atomic so it stops manufacturing the truncated member. ABSENT and UNREADABLE take the same action (start with an empty dedup list, keep answering) and are returned as different verdicts, logged apart. Deliberately NOT paged, unlike the sent-ids provenance guard: the worst case here is one replayed message answered twice, and the claim ledger still holds at-most-once execution. Control: tests/background/test_the_responder_dedup_memory_survives_a_corrupt_read.py.
.ntfy_responder_seen_hashes.json.why: A dedupe set of inbound message hashes. Append-only; no episode-scoped field.

.ntfy_responder_since.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-04, and of the three carriers on this daemon it was the one that stopped it STARTING. `_load_since` did `json.loads(...)["since"]` under `except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError)`; `null`, `[1, 2, 3]` and `["x", 2]` all PARSE, so none is a JSONDecodeError, none was ever seen by the except-clause, and the subscript one line later raised TypeError. That call is the FIRST statement of `main()` with no try above it, so a half-written watermark did not cost one poll -- the only inbound route the director has into this machine was simply absent, which is the `.sim_next_run_not_before.json` shape moved onto the channel. Measured over the whole partition against a live prior of `{"since": 1234.5}` (table in the loader's docstring). Repaired via `episode_prior.load_episode_prior`, and the partition gained a FOURTH answer: a mapping that parses but carries no `since` is `readable_without_watermark`, distinct from both absent and unreadable, because unreadable bytes are worth preserving and that record is not. UNREADABLE still resumes from now, argued not defaulted -- looking BACK re-enters `_register_inbound_and_detect_flood` and quarantines the very messages the lookback was for -- so the ACTION is the cold-start one and the ANSWER is not: `main` preserves the bytes and PAGES. That is the opposite call from the seen-hash branch beside it, deliberately: an unreadable dedup record costs one duplicate ack, an unreadable watermark costs every message sent while the daemon was down. Control: tests/background/test_the_inbound_channels_three_loaders.py
.ntfy_responder_since.json.why: A poll watermark ({"since": ts}). Advancing it is the mechanism; no alarm derives severity from its age.

.operational_layer_signal.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED. ALREADY ANSWERS THE THIRD STATE, by a different route from the rest of the sweep and a good one: `_read_operational_layer_state` screens `isinstance(st, dict)`, raises ValueError on a non-object and catches it alongside JSONDecodeError/OSError, returning `state_unavailable=True` -- a NAMED third value on the record itself rather than a verdict beside it, which callers can act on. Absent returns the same zeroed counters with `state_unavailable=False`, so absent and unreadable are distinguishable. The episode guard on top is `guard_episode` at the write. Nothing to do. CORRECTED IN PLACE: the first draft cited `episode_monotonic` alone, which is the episode question and not this one.
.operational_layer_signal.json.why: `consecutive_red` IS an episode counter and supervisor._operational_red_persistent_draw derives a priority-zero draw from it (>3 consecutive = drawable). run_operational_layer_signal read-modify-writes it, so a check that resolves to green for a reason other than a demonstrated recovery resets the episode the escalation is measured by. CLOSE CONDITION (PW4): rc == 0 AND the run reports >=1 test PASSED -- because pytest exits 0 when every selected test SKIPPED, and the operational marker selects exactly the daemon-lifecycle tests most likely to skip themselves when the daemon they drive is absent (R15 fail-open on empty). Read off the subprocess's own summary line, never off this state file. Guarded via process_run_complete.operational_layer_episode_closed -> _write_operational_layer_state(episode_closed=...). Replay proof: tests/background/test_pw4_episode_guards.py::test_op_a_green_that_ran_nothing_does_not_clear_the_red_episode (and ::test_op_a_real_green_still_clears_it for the opposite direction).

.origin_staging_sync.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. A rate-limit stamp read under a bare `except Exception -> last = 0.0`, inside a function that is fail-safe in every mode by design (Rule 0: the sync is a convenience, never a gate). An unreadable stamp costs one extra `git fetch`. Pure reader; the writer overwrites the stamp.
.origin_staging_sync.json.why: A sync watermark for origin staging pulls. Latest-value; carries no streak or episode start.

.owner-pid.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED. A bare pid written and read as text by `surgical_land` / `_pytest_root_holder`. A corrupt value fails the `os.kill(pid, 0)` liveness probe and the holder is treated as dead, which is the same answer an absent file gives and the safe one. No parse, no partition.
.owner-pid.why: Not an alarm record at all: `tools/surgical_land.py::OWNER_MARKER` holds ONE integer -- the PID that created the extract directory it sits inside -- written once, before anything else in the checkout, and never read for severity. It carries no episode-start timestamp and no consecutive-failure counter, so there is no episode any write could shorten; the sweep asks only `os.kill(pid, 0)`, a question about the CURRENT world rather than an accumulated history. It is also not durable state: it lives inside the checkout and dies with it in the same `rmtree`, so 'self-clearing' is its correct and intended behaviour rather than a defect. Hit by the lexicon on `page_`/`stale` in the sweep's own prose, not on the file's contents. Landed by 5bf1efd52 (WORKER_FINDING_THE_ONLY_LEGAL_LANDING_MOVE_LEAKS_150MB_A_KILL_2026-08-14) without a row, which is what this census is for.

.product_interleave_state.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write. ALREADY EXEMPLARY, and it is the model the rest of this sweep was measured against. `_load_interleave_state` distinguishes absent (clean slate, NOT an error) from unreadable AND malformed, and returns a NAMED reason that the digest line carries -- because, in its own words, 'a debt ledger that quietly resets always reads paid'. Live prior ['H1','H2']; each unreadable state returns [] with the reason attached. Nothing to repair.
.product_interleave_state.json.why: OPS13's pairing-debt ledger: {"owed": [harness atom ids], "last_harness", "last_product", "updated"}. No field is episode-scoped -- there is no episode-start timestamp and no consecutive-failure counter, so no write can shorten an episode. `owed` is a WORK debt, not a fault clock: it is capped at _INTERLEAVE_OWED_CAP = 3 and is paid DOWN by the machine doing the right thing, so a lost entry costs at most one forced PRODUCT draw -- and supervisor.py's own comment picks that as the direction to err in. `updated` is a latest-write watermark. Nothing reads any field for alarm SEVERITY; the consumer is product_interleave_digest_line(), which is required to emit a non-empty line on every path (the atom's own exit 4, SILENCE IS THE FAILURE). The reset paths are the opposite of self-clearing: _load_interleave_state() returns a NAMED error on an unreadable or malformed ledger and the digest line carries it, rather than resetting quietly to a state that always reads paid.

.publish_gate_state.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). ASKED. Its loader `_read_publish_gate_state` is the fail-closed shape `_read_operational_layer_state` was modelled on, and `episode_monotonic.guard_episode` holds the episode question at the write. Both asked.

REPAIRED, and the two readers needed OPPOSITE repairs, which is why grading four readers off one sibling could never have worked: the scorecard is a pure reader and now drops the line and PUBLISHES the drop as `unreadable_log_lines` (its `log_entry_count` reaches the Proof door via generate_proof_data, and a quietly shrunken track record is a plausible number nobody notices); the append guard REFUSES, because skipping an unreadable line drops that day out of `existing_dates` and a re-run then appends a SECOND row for the same day -- the duplicate its one-entry-per-day rule exists to forbid. Control: tests/background/test_the_jsonl_carriers_claim_was_reasoned_from_a_sibling_and_one_of_five_was_wrong.py, seven named mutations verified to red it.

Flagged because record/record_gate_run are on the publish FAILURE path and process_run_complete transitively reads the file, but it is an append-only JSONL carrying no episode-scoped field -- no episode-start timestamp, no consecutive-failure counter -- so no write can shorten an episode (same shape as run_history.json and live_decisions_log.jsonl). The alarm is an R5 band TRANSITION against the immediately preceding row; appending never erases the history that transition is read from. NOT guarded, deliberately: the `real` guard is append-or-monotonic on an episode field this control does not have, and inventing a close condition nobody chose is the reflex-guarding the _scope_note above forbids. SEPARATELY DEFECTIVE, and filed rather than folded in here: record_gate_run is called with the elapsed time of RED runs too, and a `-x` gate aborts early (276s and 392s on 2026-08-10 vs ~500s green), so failures append short durations that inflate headroom and can flip the band toward `ok`. That corrupts the trend STATISTIC; it does not shorten an episode, so it is a measurement-validity defect and not this class -- see WORKER_FINDING_THE_DURATION_SERIES_RECORDS_ABORTED_RUNS_2026-08-10.md.

publish_provenance.json.why: `paused_since` IS an episode-start timestamp, and it is rendered as the SEVERITY of the loudest alarm surface this machine has -- a public banner reading 'Verification paused since T' (publish_provenance.banner_line, published by process_run_complete._publish_provenance_banner on exactly the cycles the numbers must not move). record_paused is on the gate-RED path and writes the same file that banner reads, so a re-stamp every red cycle would page a 25-hour pause as 'paused since 30 seconds ago' -- the .publish_gate_state.json instance wearing the opposite coat, and on the visitor's page rather than the director's phone. ALREADY GUARDED, and guarded in its own module rather than through background/episode_monotonic.py: record_paused stamps only `if not state.get('paused_since')`, and the sole writer that clears it is record_verified, reachable only from a publish that COMPLETED with the scoped gate green. That close is independent of this file (the publisher's own return path), which is the anti-tautology property the other five real rows are held to. Replay proof: tests/background/test_publish_provenance.py::test_paused_since_is_stamped_once_not_re_stamped_every_cycle (opposite direction: ::test_recovery_clears_the_pause_and_advances). A second, stronger property sits alongside the episode guard and is mutation-proven separately: record_paused cannot write showing_run or last_verified AT ALL, so no failure path can advance the freshness claim -- tests/background/test_publish_provenance.py::test_a_pause_cannot_move_the_served_run_by_a_byte.

retired_paths_served.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). `run()` read the prior under `except ValueError`, so `[1,2,3]` and `"abc"` reached `transitions`' `(previous or {}).get` and raised AttributeError. `null` answered CORRECTLY BY ACCIDENT -- `None or {}` is `{}` -- which is exactly what made the other two look impossible; a partition member passing for the wrong reason is worth more attention than one failing. Repaired via `load_episode_prior`, behind a new named `_load_previous_state` seam: `run()` refuses without a real site checkout, so a control written against `run` cannot reach the load, and the first draft of the control called `load_episode_prior` itself and SURVIVED the mutation restoring the old read -- it was asserting the helper against itself. No preserve: `current` is recomputed in full from the edge rows, so the write loses nothing; an unreadable prior costs one re-report of every live ghost, which is noisy and not wrong.
retired_paths_served.json.why: docs/observability/retired_paths_served.json -- `tools/retired_paths_still_served.py`'s snapshot of which retired paths the edge is still serving. It is state-file-shaped and the census matches it on that shape, but it cannot self-clear: every verdict is RE-DERIVED from `docs/observability/edge_traffic.jsonl` on each run (`still_served = 200 in hours[last]`, tools/retired_paths_still_served.py:261), and that traffic log is append-only and written by the collector. Delete this file entirely and the next run reproduces the same verdicts from the traffic. The hazard this census exists to catch is a state file whose RESET silently ends an episode that never ended; here a clear is an OBSERVED 404 at the edge, not a reset -- the module's own docstring argues exactly that ('derived, never remembered'), and it was built because a hand-enumerated ghost list missed a ninth path. Dispositioned by the delivery seat 2026-08-25 because it was the last undispositioned hit and was refusing every commit that touched this register; if the derivation ever stops reading the traffic log and starts trusting the previous snapshot, this verdict is wrong and must become `real`.

run_history.json.loader: SWEPT 2026-09-05 (delivery-seat sweep of the 34 rows that carried no `loader` field). RANKED FIRST AND IT WAS THE WORST ROW ON THE CENSUS. `append_run_history` is a read-modify-write and `count_run_history_total` publishes its length as the Project tab's 'Sim runs' KPI. Measured against a LIVE PRIOR of 100 runs: truncated/empty -> `history = []` then wrote a ONE-entry list over all 100, so the published KPI fell 100 -> 1 with nothing able to notice. `null` PARSES, so the `except (JSONDecodeError, ValueError)` never saw it and `len(None)` raised TypeError out of BOTH dashboard readers, whose contract is literally 'or [] if invalid' -- that raise lands in the dashboard build. `{"a": 1}` / `[1,2,3]` / `"abc"` raised AttributeError in the append, swallowed by `_process`'s blanket handler as 'Run insights generation skipped', losing the run from history for good -- AND the KPI still answered, publishing 1 / 3 / 3, because `len()` is happy to count the characters of a corrupt string. A FABRICATED FIGURE ON THE DIRECTOR'S OWN SURFACE is the finding here, not the crash. Repaired via `episode_prior.load_list_prior(..., item_type=dict)` in all three, plus `preserve_unreadable` in the writer. The absent-vs-unreadable CONFLATION in the rendered figure is left deliberately: both show 0, because the KPI counts runs we can account for and a record we cannot parse accounts for none. What is no longer conflated is the disposal of the bytes. Control: tests/background/test_the_census_rows_that_had_never_been_asked_the_loader_question.py
